questions.q: What question does Renee ask after the presentation?
options: Why did the correlation rule take so long to fire
How do we know this is the only firewall rule with this problem
Why wasn't the vendor rule deleted entirely
When will the Advanced tier begin
questions.explain: Renee's follow-up asks whether the same class of gap exists elsewhere, not just whether this one instance is fixed.

questions.q: Why does "we fixed this one" fail to fully answer Renee's question?
options: Because the rule was never actually fixed
Because fixing the caught rule says nothing about whether the same kind of gap exists elsewhere, unchecked
Because Renee does not trust Mara
Because the fix was not validated
questions.explain: A single fixed instance doesn't address the systemic question of whether other rules share the same gap.

questions.q: What does Part 1 of Mara's answer -- the one-time check -- establish?
options: That no firewall rules exist at all
A completed audit of every other current firewall rule's scope against its documented justification, finding no other instance of this gap right now
A promise to check rules sometime in the future
That the vendor's rule was the only rule ever created
questions.explain: The one-time audit is a checked fact about the present state of every rule, not a future promise.

questions.q: What does Part 2 -- the standing control -- add that Part 1 alone doesn't cover?
options: Nothing; Part 1 alone is sufficient
An ongoing, checkable process (per-change gate plus periodic review) that keeps covering new and existing rules going forward
A guarantee that no mistake will ever happen again
A requirement that Renee personally review every firewall rule
questions.explain: Part 1 answers 'right now'; Part 2 answers 'and going forward,' using the control introduced in Lesson 12.

questions.q: Why does the lesson distinguish evidence from reassurance?
options: They mean the same thing in this context
Reassurance ('we'll be more careful') gives nothing to verify; evidence (a completed audit, a named ongoing control) gives Renee something checkable
Reassurance is always more persuasive to a compliance officer
Evidence is only relevant to IT Directors, not compliance officers
questions.explain: A compliance officer's job is to require verifiable evidence, not take confidence on faith.
